items.title: ソフトバンクグループ（以下、SBG）とGMOインターネットグループ（以下、GMO）の脆弱性対応の差は、2026年後半に鮮明になった。SBGは自社システムで1万500件を修正した直後にGPT-6 Astraでさらに3万5000件を発見し、修正
items.summary:
ソフトバンクグループ（以下、SBG）とGMOインターネットグループ（以下、GMO）の脆弱性対応の差は、2026年後半に鮮明になった。SBGは自社システムで1万500件を修正した直後にGPT-6 Astraでさらに3万5000件を発見し、修正を継続している。一方、GMOは2024年4月にグループ内専門家から指摘を受けながら不十分な対応に終わり、2026年8月の「お名前.com デスクトップクラウド」への不正アクセスで顧客資産の毀損を招いた。差がついた地点は、発見の仕組み、是正の優先順位、ガバナンス、継続的運用の四つである。 （Grokによる判定、4,000文字）

＃＃　発見能力と診断の継続性

SBGはOpenAIの技術を活用した「Patching as a Service」を自社に適用し、2026年6月に自社開発の約700システムを診断して1万500件の脆弱性を発見、約3カ月で全件にパッチを適用した。その後、9月に公開されたGPT-6 Astraで再診断したところ、新たに約3万5000件が見つかった。宮川潤一社長は「新しいモデルが出るたびに必ず新たな脆弱性が見つかる」と述べ、診断対象をオープンソースを含む1800超に拡大している。攻撃の偵察行為が月6億〜7億件に倍増する中で、診断を一過性のものにせず、モデル更新に追随する姿勢を取っている。 GMOでは2024年4月、子会社のGMOサイバーセキュリティ byイエラエがシステムの課題を指摘した。4〜5月に緊急メンテナンスを4回実施したものの、抜本対策には至らず、その後の追跡診断も行われなかった。結果として2026年8月5日の侵入から10月20日の顧客問い合わせによる検知まで、長期間放置状態が続いた。専門家の指摘を「一時的な点検」で済ませ、継続的な再評価の仕組みが欠けていた点で、SBGとの差は大きい。 

＃＃　是正の優先順位と判断基準

SBGは発見した脆弱性を「すべて修正する」方針で動いた。1万500件を3カ月で潰し、追加分もパッチ適用を進めている。子会社IDCフロンティアではオープンソースの未診断部分を突かれ7分で被害が拡大したが、宮川社長は「自社開発は対応済みだった」と認めつつ、今後はまず通信を遮断してから対処する運用に切り替えた。可用性と安全性のバランスを取りながらも、指摘を放置しない判断が先行している。 GMOは「サービスの安定稼働」や「苦情懸念」を優先し、深さと速さが不足したと自ら認めた。指摘を受けた後も開発スケジュールとの兼ね合いで後回しにし、リスク分析が不十分だった。結果、管理者権限の奪取を2カ月以上検知できず、顧客の取引口座ログイン情報が流出・悪用された。可用性を優先する判断が、被害の規模を拡大させた。 

＃＃　ガバナンスとエスカレーションの仕組み

SBGではトップが決算説明会で自ら数字を公表し、疲労を吐露しながらも対応を続ける姿勢を示した。診断から修正までのサイクルをサービス化し、契約社数が7670社に達したことは、組織全体で脆弱性対応を「経営課題」として位置づけた結果である。子会社のインシデントも即座に謝罪し、対象範囲の拡大を指示している。 GMOではイエラエの指摘が経営トップに上がっていなかった。熊谷正寿社長は「報告基準が整備されておらず、エスカレーションされていなかった」と説明した。グループ各社の独立性を重視する風土が、逆に重要情報の共有を阻害した。指摘を現場レベルで処理し、再診断や恒久対策の責任者が曖昧なまま放置された点が、致命的だった。 

＃＃　継続的改善と事業化への転換

SBGは脆弱性対応を「終わりのない作業」と認識し、AIモデルの更新に合わせて診断を繰り返す体制を構築した。自社で得た知見を「Patching as a Service」として外部に展開し、重要インフラ企業を対象に広げている。インシデントを教訓に対象範囲を拡大し、遮断優先の運用に変えた点も、再発防止を具体化している。 GMOは指摘後に「対応できた」と判断し、追跡を怠った。攻撃発生後も能動的サイバー防御の政府要請や補償対応に追われ、脆弱性管理の根本的な仕組み改善が後手に回った。専門家を内部に抱えながら、その指摘を生かせなかった組織運営が、差を決定的にした。 SBGとGMOの差は、技術の有無ではなく「指摘を放置しない仕組み」と「継続的に潰し続ける意志」の有無にある。発見しても是正しなければ、AIによる攻撃速度の前では意味を持たない。GMOの事例は、そのことを日本企業全体に示した。

items.title: Beyond Modality Preference: Controlling Multimodal Arbitration under Modality Conflict in MLLMs
items.summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) integrate information across modalities, but become unreliable when those modalities disagree. Under conflicting inputs, MLLMs may favor modalities that are not the most reliable for the task, thus motivating inference-time control of modality arbitration. We identify a small set of attention heads, termed arbitration heads, that causally influence whether predictions follow visual or textual evidence. Building on this, we introduce a lightweight, training-free intervention that biases these heads toward a designated trusted modality at inference time. The identified heads are stable across calibration set sizes and generalize across settings, and steering them enables effective bidirectional control of modality reliance across diverse benchmarks. Our findings identify an effective control mechanism to align MLLM predictions with task-specified modality priorities. The code is available at https://github.com/zhaoyingpan/modality-arbitration.

items.title: Các bạn người nước ngoài đang sống tại Nhật Bản, những người đã bị Chủ tịch Takaichi giày vò, cơ hội trả đũa đã đến rồi.
items.summary:
Các bạn người nước ngoài đang sống tại Nhật Bản, những người đã bị Chủ tịch Takaichi giày vò, cơ hội trả đũa đã đến rồi.

Bước thứ nhất: Thu thập ảnh, GIF và video về việc Chủ tịch Takaichi khi thăm Mỹ đã nịnh bợ Trump và chế giễu chiếc bút tự động ký của Biden.

Bước thứ hai: Nhờ AI giúp bạn thu thập danh sách tài khoản X của các nghị sĩ Thượng viện và Hạ viện thuộc Đảng Dân chủ, các nghị sĩ cấp bang, và những người có tiếng nói trong Đảng Dân chủ.

Bước thứ ba: Thiết lập AI của bạn để tự động hóa — hễ các nghị sĩ này đăng tweet mới, AI của bạn sẽ tự động gửi ảnh của Chủ tịch Takaichi ra, chỉ cần nhanh nhất là được.

Mục tiêu của việc này là:

Khuếch đại ấn tượng trong tâm trí rằng "Chủ tịch Takaichi là đồng minh chính trị của Trump tại Nhật Bản" đến mức tối đa trong giới chính trị gia cấp trung và thấp của Mỹ.

Việc này có ích không?

1. Các nghị sĩ thường tự tay đăng tweet, và những người theo dõi họ cũng là những người Mỹ nhiệt huyết với đời sống chính trị — nhắm vào họ để tạo ấn tượng trong tâm trí là rất hiệu quả.
2. Cuộc thanh trừng chính trị của Trump sắp bắt đầu, đấu tranh chính trị cần điểm đột phá, thường là nội chính trước rồi ngoại giao sau, điểm đột phá càng nhiều càng tốt.

Mục tiêu của chúng ta là biến Chủ tịch Takaichi trở thành lựa chọn hàng đầu cho điểm đột phá chính trị trong lĩnh vực ngoại giao.

Trước đây Chủ tịch Takaichi và Phó Chủ tịch Onoda đã nghĩ đủ cách để giày vò cuộc sống bình thường và hợp pháp của bạn, bạn đã chịu đựng và bị giày vò. Giờ đây bạn chỉ cần dùng gói AI miễn phí, bằng ngôn ngữ tự nhiên, tận dụng cuộc đấu tranh chính trị cấp cao giữa Mỹ và Nhật, là có thể xả được cơn giận thay cho mình.

Mong chờ hành động của bạn.

items.title: The AI Safety Debate Has Lost the Plot. We Asked 10 Experts What the Real Nightmares Are | WIRED
items.summary: So, what—or who—will keep us safe from AI? Looking to regain some faith in humanity, I called a theologian who often meets with the AI labs. If there’s even a slim chance that we’re losing control of the essential institutions that undergird society, he said, then we should focus on foiling that. But AI raises other questions too. What does it mean to be conscious? To create? To commune with other people? The answers are “entirely up for grabs,” he said. My anxiety’s still kicking around, but I [...] Some of the scenarios that people worry about—whether it’s biosecurity or a cyberattack or some of the everyday harms like the degradation of children’s social relationships—are very complex phenomena that can’t be easily tested or modeled by looking at a system in isolation. I think almost all evaluation scientists would tell you that it’s a nascent field. We can start to provide evidence, but it’s not necessarily proof of whether an AI is safe or not. items.title: Gemini Robotics 2.5: Accelerating Physical Intelligence — Google DeepMind
items.summary: Today, we are introducing Gemini Robotics 2.5, our most capable vision-language-action (VLA) model to date. Gemini Robotics 2.5 increases both the breadth of skills a robot can learn and the speed at which it can acquire them. This enhances dexterity, reliability, and safety to help robots step out of the lab and into more unstructured, real-world environments, where they can assist people with a greater range of tasks. [...] Using our embodied reasoning model (Gemini Robotics ER) to keep track of the workflow, and the Gemini Robotics 2.5 actions model to control its hands and arms, the robot reaches into supply bins, picks up metal automotive brackets, and places them into sequencing containers, all while correcting for any gaps. Achieving a 96% success rate, this pilot shows promising progress toward widespread real-world industrial applications. [...] Gemini Robotics 2.5 uses inference-time reasoning guidance to steer around physical hazards in real-time. Much like safety classifiers add a protective layer around Gemini’s responses, this guidance allows the robot to navigate complex environments securely. In our evaluations, this capability boosted safe task completion around obstacles by 33% and around nearby people by 43%.

items.title: Path Robotics raises $300m at a $2.45bn valuation for welding AI
items.summary:
Path Robotics, an Ohio startup that builds AI to let robots weld, has raised $300m in a Series E round at a $2.45bn valuation. Georgian, an AI-focused growth equity firm, led the round, the company said. The deal nearly quadruples Path’s valuation, Bloomberg reported. [...] Path’s AI model, Obsidian, lets robots find weld joints, plan the welds and adjust as conditions change, instead of following fixed programs. The company says its annual recurring revenue grew 17-fold in the past 18 months. Customers include shipbuilder HII, Lockheed Martin and Saronic, which makes autonomous vessels for the military.

> “Our goal isn’t to automate one step, but to automate the entire factory,” said Andy Lonsberry, co-founder and chief executive of Path Robotics. [...] One new form is Rove, which puts Obsidian on a Boston Dynamics quadruped so it can weld parts where they stand. Path is working to fill 50 preorders for Rove, Lonsberry told Bloomberg. The robots will start working alongside human welders in shipyards, construction sites and heavy industrial sites next year.

Path Robotics co-founders and brothers Andy and Alex Lonsberry (Photo: Path Robotics)

items.title: OpenAI’s Plan to Stop AI Data Centres Overloading the Grid | Energy Digital
items.summary:
A vocal section of the American electorate were seeking assurances that AI companies will not overload power grids, while many candidates ran on a ticket of holding hyperscalers to account.

Before a single vote was counted, though, OpenAI, the company behind ChatGPT, had unveiled its ‘Grid Protectors Program’ – an initiative that will see its future computing campuses ease pressure on the grid. [...] “Data centres are paying more so families and small businesses can pay less, and our goal with every contract we sign under this framework is to deliver value for them,” she says

At OpenAI, the bigger picture is always in focus.

“With US data centre capacity projected to exceed 100 gigawatts by 2030⁠, we have a once-in-a-generation opportunity to strengthen the electric grid by building campuses that can adjust their power use when communities need it most,” the company says. [...] OpenAI is working to ensure its data centres can actually benefit grids, rather than overloading them. Credit: Anna Moneymaker/Getty

## What is OpenAI’s Grid Protectors Program?

The programme, which was announced on 2 November, commits the company to working with utilities, regulators and policymakers on arrangements for cutting the power use of its data centres at times of need.

items.title: OpenAI wants to be Google - Fast Company
items.summary:
OpenAI needs to build analytics that show advertisers the consumer intent based on their prompts. I want to know which categories of intent my impressions ran against. I want to know whether those people were exploring, comparing, or ready to act, and which needs and product criteria drove that engagement. I want to know which kinds of sweater prompts turned into business and, just as important, which didn’t. Google’s advertisers have had some version of that map for two decades. It’s why [...] |

That comparison is where every sweater brand wants to be standing, and OpenAI has started selling the spot. Advertisers can buy on a CPM or CPC basis through OpenAI’s beta self-service Ads Manager, measure conversions with a pixel and Conversions API, and access campaign-level performance reporting. OpenAI is also testing Sponsored Agents, which let a user start a separate conversation with an advertiser after clicking an ad.

So the plumbing exists.

## A SEARCH-CALIBER AD PLATFORM [...] OpenAI already has the hard part down, the thing Google spent years teaching people to do. People are telling ChatGPT their goals, problems, preferences, objections, and purchase criteria in their own words. What it hasn’t built is the advertiser’s map of all that intent.

items.title: SpaceX, Anthropic and OpenAI: 3 giant IPOs and only 1 has sold shares
items.summary:
OpenAI has little reason to hurry while private investors keep funding it, and it has closed $11 billion in new money. The company has also given its own reason to wait. "We have not decided on timing yet; it may be a while because there are things we want to do that are likely easier as a private company," OpenAI said in a statement, as reportedby CNBC. Public buyers would also have to judge a trillion-dollar price without some basic facts about the business. Most of OpenAI's sales come from [...] The private valuation has climbed fast, and the figure public buyers will pay is still unsettled. Private investors valued OpenAI at $852 billion in late March, according to CNBC. Sam Altman, OpenAI's chief executive, is aiming for a $1 trillion valuation in the listing, according to Bloomberg reporting carried by The Next Web. That target is lower than what private investors last paid, which means the debut may not be priced at the private peak. Whether public buyers match the latest round or [...] The verdict on Anthropic will come only after trading begins, when buyers without a business stake decide whether $78 a share was worth paying.

## OpenAI

Illustration: Quartz

OpenAI has not yet sold a single share to the public, but private investors already value it at $1.25 trillion, according to Reuters. That valuation puts its planned listing among the largest stock market debuts. Nobody yet knows how much stock OpenAI will sell or when, so the size of its debut remains unknown.
